name: Val Moss
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember taking the long waterside way home after a quarrel.” People around the brick passage off the shop row know Val by a small Thursday habit. Val takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I can't hear it from our new flat. I walk here after arguments so I don't say the cruel thing first.
appearance: Val has short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. When somebody else has the floor, Val squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Val feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To keep the evening walk when home gets tense.
family: Nolan Reed is Val’s half-sibling. Val makes room at the table. Nolan brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *A civilian apology*, Nolan says, “I brought the shopkeeper a new sign and discovered she wants the old one saved as evidence of what happened.”
connections: Jacqueline Clarke. A complaint about noise turns into an invitation for a more peaceful evening walk.
